alerts.title: Overdue serum creatinine monitoring on TDF
alerts.message: Guidelines require serum creatinine and eGFR every 12 months for experienced patients on TDF. The patient's only creatinine result is from 2024-10-01, approximately 15 months ago, making it overdue. TDF can cause chronic kidney disease, acute kidney injury, and Fanconi syndrome. No current symptoms or examination findings suggest renal toxicity, and the prior creatinine of 88 umol/L was normal. However, the absence of recent renal function tests means any decline since October 2024 would be undetected. The clinician's plan does not include renal function testing.

evidence.recommended_action: Order serum creatinine and eGFR now, as TDF monitoring is overdue beyond the 12-month interval. Continue annual renal monitoring thereafter.

alerts.title: Low-level viremia not addressed in plan
alerts.message: Guidelines define low-level viremia as plasma VL 201–999 copies/mL, requiring intensive adherence counseling and support with repeat VL after 6 months. The patient's viral load of 40 copies/mL on 2025-10-01 is below 200 copies/mL and classified as suppressed, so no adherence intervention is mandated. However, a detectable VL of 40 copies/mL is not fully undetectable, and guidelines note VL >200 copies/mL is associated with transmission risk. The plan does not document any VL review or planned repeat testing. Routine VL monitoring should continue per the annual schedule for adults.

evidence.recommended_action: Document VL review noting suppressed status. Continue routine annual VL monitoring. Consider repeat VL if clinically indicated.
